audits.title: Fishery products

recommendations.text: Improvement of the co-ordinating and supervisory role of the GVI This should include at least the following points: - Written procedures for the Provincial and County Veterinary Inspectorates. - Check lists for initial approval of establishments. - Procedures for the routine checks of the establishments - Check lists for the routine checks of establishments. - Training of staff of the Provincial and County Veterinary Inspectorates

Introduction of initial approval and annual routine checks of factory vessels This should include at least the following points: - Full initial inspection of all EU approved factory vessels. The official records, including the official approval of corrective actions, should be kept at the offices of the Competent Authority; - Annual routine checks of all EU approved factory vessels, comprising a physical check, a check of the records of the own checks and official supervisory laboratory tests. The official records, including the official approval of corrective actions, should be kept at the offices of the Competent Authority; - An HACCP-plan approved by the Competent Authority should be in place on all EU approved factory vessels. Only factory vessels that are fully checked within one year prior to the establishment of the final list and from which the Competent Authority has approved the correction of the deficiencies can be included.

Laboratory service It is recommended to formalise the relation between the PIWet and the GVI/CVO, at least the annual working programme of the PIWet should be approved by the CVO. 12 The Competent Authority should inform the Commission services about the finalisation of the modification of the Polish Norms (PN) to make them equivalent to the ISO and EN standards

Residue controls New legislation on residues, should come into force as soon as possible, but 1 February 2000 the latest. The relevant veterinary drugs and chemicals, should be included in the Residue Monitoring Programme.

Changes in the approval and checks of the establishments The following is recommended: - Correction of the deficiencies observed in the structure and the standards of operating hygiene in the establishments, and in the implementation of the HACCP system. - Correction of the deficiencies observed in the official supervision of the establishments and the record keeping by the County/Provincial Inspectorate. - During the annual checks on establishments it should be ensured that deficiencies similar to those observed during the mission are corrected.
Approval and checks of fish farms Recommendations will depend on the assessment of the additional information, including on "own check" programme and on animal health controls.

Written guarantees Written guarantees should be forwarded to the European Commission services in respect of the points listed above; where appropriate a detailed timetable should be included. 7.2. To the Commission Services - After receiving, evaluating and considering that the written guarantees sought from the Polish competent authority are satisfactory, the Commission services should propose to Member States that Poland be placed on the list I of Annex of the amended Commission Decision 97/296/EC and that a Commission Decision be adopted. - To consider a follow up mission paying particular attention to factory vessels and fish farms. -------------- 13

audits.title: Public health issues

recommendations.text: The Polish authorities should take urgent action to improve the quality of the veterinary health certificates and ensure that the certificates reflect the requirements of current Community legislation;

The Polish authorities should take action to : 6.1.2.1. ensure the correct implementation of the new tasks assigned to the provincial veterinary officers; 6.1.2.2. transpose into National law the Community legislation on the collection, production and transport of milk in order to comply with the "Acquis Communautaire"; 6.1.2.3. approve formally (i.e. issue the formal approval letters) the plants notified to the European Commission as fulfilling the EC requirements; 6.1.2.4. ensure there is proper health marking of wild game and meat products; 12 6.1.2.5. rectify the plant deficiencies found during the mission, in particular the failure to approve heat treatment equipment in the milk factories; 6.1.2.6. approve by the CCA the procedures used for separate processing of milk of EU quality ("extra class") upon satisfactory report provided by the supervising veterinary services. This approval should form part of the notification to the Commission of the approval of the establishment as meeting EU standard; 6.1.2.7. fully implement the EC standards for potable water; 6.1.2.8. speed up the appointment of the Milk Reference Laboratory; 6.1.2.9. ensure that milk samples taken from the processing plants are analysed at officially approved laboratories (official checks and the plants' "own checks"). The CCA should establish the criteria for approval, and inform the Commission thereof. A laboratory accreditation programme should be put in place. A report indicating the actions taken or the time needed to rectify the deficiencies described under points 6.1.2.1. ­ 6.1.2.9. should be submitted to the Commission within two months of receiving the final report. The Commission must be informed when the deficiencies are rectified especially those on the transposition of Community legislation into Polish national law. 6.2. To the European Commission: The Commission Services should consider: 6.2.1. after receiving satisfactory guarantees, confirming the approval of eight Polish milk-processing plants, approved by the CA and further approval of the five milk processing plants listed according to the Commission Decision 97/252/EC as amended by 1999/52/EC; 6.2.2. informing the Polish CCA once the approval procedure has been satisfactorily completed; 6.2.3. taking action to ensure that Member States : - do not require certification and/or health conditions in excess of those laid down in the relevant Community legislation; - accept only veterinary health certificates reflecting the requirements of current Community legislation; 6.2.4. determining the reasons for the delay of accreditation of the third laboratory involved in the PHARE programme; 6.2.5 checking the legal basis and establishing a certificate model concerning salmonella examination in fresh meat and poultry meat imported from third countries into Sweden and Finland. 13
recommendations.legal_basis: and establishing a certificate model concerning salmonella examination in fresh meat and poultry meat imported from third countries into Sweden and Finland. 13

audits.title: Radioactive contamination in imported mushrooms

recommendations.text: The Polish Competent Authority responded that the general modernisation of the laboratories and equipment will be continued as far as necessary financial resources are provided or granted.

The Polish Competent Authority responded that a comprehensive and uniform written quality assurance system regarding the gamma spectrometric measurement of radioactive contamination in foodstuffs or mushrooms for export is projected to be developed together with all laboratories involved with the export certification by September 2000.

The Polish Competent Authority responded that the laboratories envisage an accreditation as indicated in the export certificate for agricultural products, if an additional source of funding is found. 9.2. Response to points 8.1.2. ­ 8.1.4. The Polish Competent Authority pointed out that improvements of valid legislation and procedures, concerning the Agricultural and Food Quality Inspection activities could be made after acceptation of Minister of Agriculture and Rural Development. Furthermore, Polish Competent Authority stated that written assurances and deadlines for all adaptation work could be send after the final decisions regarding the reorganisation of Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development, which might be a time- consuming procedure. 20

audits.title: Production of fresh meat, meat preparations and meat products

recommendations.text: Keep the Commission Services informed about the progress of the new "Veterinary Framework Act" and associated regulations.
Include veterinary certification for meat products, minced meat, meat preparations and casings in the action plan for the improvement of certificates recommended in report SANCO/1018/2000.
Introduce comprehensive veterinary checks at Border Inspection Posts, as laid down in existing EU legislation.
Establish a legal basis for the National Reference Laboratory and certify the approved laboratories.
recommendations.legal_basis: for the National Reference Laboratory and certify the approved laboratories.

recommendations.text: Staff levels should be increased to meet the operational requirements of the veterinary service.

Implement clear written guidelines describing the procedures for suspending (with time limits) and withdrawing approval for EU listed establishments to ensure that the European Commission is kept informed of changes to lists of approved establishments.
Ensure that there is adequate day to day veterinary supervision in establishments so that immediate action can be taken when a non compliance with EU standards is detected.
Additional training should be provided to Official Veterinary Surgeons so that they can more effectively supervise the implementation of the establishment CCP/HACCP plan.
The EU health mark should only be used when products fulfil all the requirements of the Directive and then be applied in the proper manner.

Rectify the establishment deficiencies noted during the mission. A report indicating the actions taken or to be taken and including a timetable for completing the recommendations in points 8.1.5 to 8.1.10, should be submitted to the Commission within two months of receiving the final report. This report should also include a concise written description of the progress made on points 8.1.1 to 8.1.4. 14 8.2. To the Commission services: The Commission Services should consider: 1. Confirming the approval of the 2 integrated establishments and the casings establishment inspected during the mission, upon receipt of satisfactory written guarantees. 2. Carrying out a follow up mission to evaluate the performance of the CCA when it has had some experience operating within the new structure (see 5.1.4) and preferably after the adoption of the revised Veterinary Framework Act. This mission should, in any case, take place not later than the second half of 2001. It will focus particularly upon the structure, resources and operation of veterinary controls and on health certification procedures in this sector. ADDENDUM TO MISSION REPORT 1068/2000 Competent Authority response to the recommendations in the report The Competent Authority has provided a satisfactory response to recommendations (8.1.2, 8.1.4 and 8.1.7 - 8.1.10). They have given an initial response to the remai s and have given an undertaking to keep the FVO informed about their progress. It is anticipated that a timetable will be submitted (within two months of receiving the final report) for recommendations 8.1.5 and 8.1.6 and a detailed update on the progress of the new "Veterinary Framework Act" which effects recommendations 8.1.3 and 8.1.4. The Competent Authority has also indicated the action taken in response to specific deficiencies identified within the report (see 5.3.1, 5.3.2.1, and 5.3.2.2). 15 GENERAL VETERINARY INSPECTORATE Prime Minister Appoints the CVO upon the Minister's of Agriculture and Rural Development request CHIEF VETERINARY OFFICER (CVO) Expert for Biological DEPUTY CVO & DIRECTOR GENERALE Material General Veterinary Inspectorate Expert for Laboratory Animal Infectious Diseases Diagnostic Control Division Expert for Animal Hygiene of Foodstuffs of Welfare Animal Information Origin and Feedstuffs Division Technology Legal and Organising Division European Integration and Foreign Co-operation Division Administrative Division Voïvodship VETERINARY OFFICER Voïvodship Veterinary Inspectorate (16) Office of the Voïvodship Veterinary Officer (16) Border Veterinary Inspectorates (27) Voïvodship Veterinary (16) Laboratories and their branches DISTRICT VETERINARY OFFICER (291) Distict Veterinary Inspector16ate

audits.title: Poultry meat

recommendations.text: Recommendations to the Commission services The Commission should develop guidelines in regard to the production of fresh poultry meat.

Recommendations to the Central Competent Authorities of Poland. The competent authorities should urgently rectify the deficiencies in regard to the technical equipment for stunning of birds and its supervision and assure that in all the other establishments not visited during the mission those deficiencies are being rectified in cases where they exist. The competent authorities should take care that the theoretical knowledge of the official veterinarians in the establishments is being kept up to date. 22 ADDENDUM TO MISSION REPORT DG(SANCO)1202/2000 Competent Authority's (CA) response to the recommendations in the report The CA has stated, in their letter of 17 January 2001, that the following actions have been or will be taken to rectify the shortcomings indicated during the FVO inspection: · The shortcomings noted in the establishments visited have been rectified. The CVO has also ordered the Provincial Veterinary Officers to ensure that similar shortcomings are rectified in all other poultry meat establishments. · The CVO has issued new orders to establish proper documentation of veterinary supervision of animal welfare during transport. · As regards animal welfare at slaughter action has been taken to redesign the existing stunners in poultry meat establishments to overcome the technical problems identified during the inspection. Minimum requirements for electrical parameters have been established. Training of official veterinarians in supervision of animal welfare at slaughter is organised. Before the commencement of the next slaughter season of ducks and geese every establishment will be inspected to ensure that stunning is properly carried out. Moreover, the CVO has sent a letter to the manufacturers of stunning equipment addressing the technical problems. 23

audits.title: Classical Swine Fever, Milk and milk-based products

recommendations.text: To implement the relevant provisions of EC legislation into Polish legislation, once the new Veterinary Law comes into force. Concerning controls of Classical Swine Fever :
To update the CSF Monitoring Programme in light of this mission's findings and conclusions, and to forward the results to the Commission's services once the programme has been completed.
To prepare at national level a Contingency Plan for CSF in domestic pigs and wild boars.
To prepare forms to accompany the samples on the basis of information needed by the epidemiologists. Concerning the milk sector :
To ensure that milk and milk products exported to the EU fully comply with all the provisions of the relevant Community legislation.

To ensure that deficiencies found during this mission are addressed in all EU-approved establishments. To submit, within two months of receiving the final report, an action plan indicating the action proposed or already taken by the Competent Authorities to address the conclusions and recommendations of this report. This plan should include deadlines by which the proposed action will be completed. 8.2. To the Commission Services 8.2.1. To analyse the results of the CSF monitoring programme, and to take these into account when considering whether Poland should be approved as suitable for Member States to import fresh pig meat and wild boar meat. 8.2.2. To retain Poland on the provisional list of countries authorised for the export of milk and milk-based products, provided that the competent authorities of Poland respond in a satisfactory manner within the deadline to the above mentioned recommendations. 38 ADDENDUM TO MISSION REPORT DG(SANCO)/3197/2001 Competent Authority response to the recommendations in the report The Polish authorities responded to the draft report in a letter dated 23 July 2001. They offered a number of clarifying comments, which are reflected in the final report, as well as undertakings in relation to certain of the report's conclusions and recommendations. In addition, details of CSF test results for the period 1 January - 30 June 2001 were provided. 39

audits.title: Eggs and egg products

recommendations.text: Competent authority performance The CCA should improve the co-ordination with and carry out supervisory visits to the regions in order to be able to evaluate their performances.

Food safety controls The CCA should rectify all the deficiencies found and referred to under the different conclusions in Section 6.3 above, in particular: · The egg packing centres should be authorised and supervised in the case of exports of eggs to the EU. · Own check programmes and their supervision need to be improved. · Supervision on egg products unfit for human consumption has to be improved. 22 The CCA should inform the Commission of the progress and result of the measures taken, within two months following the receipt of the final report, including a timetable for completion of measures and actions still outstanding at that time. The certification and the export of non-pasteurised (non-treated) egg products should be stopped immediately and the CA should provide the relevant guaranties the Commission Services within two weeks after receipt of the draft report.24 9.2. To the Commission Services If the CA of Poland do not provide the necessary guarantees with regard to the export of non-treated egg products within the given deadline the Commission services should consider to de-list Poland from the Commission Decision 94/278/EC25 (list of third countries from which the Member States authorise imports of certain products subject to Council Directive 92/118/EEC) for egg products; 24 Guarantees have not yet been received at the time this final report was issued. 25 OJ No L 120 of 11/5/1994, p. 44 23 10. ADDENDUM TO MISSION REPORT DG(SANCO)/3425/2001 Central Competent Authority's response to the recommendations in the report In their communications to the FVO dated 22/11/2001 and 1/03/2002, the CCA declared that the following actions and measures have been taken, in response to the remarks and recommendations in the report: · With regard to recommendation 9.1: All the shortcomings in the establishments visited during the mission have been eliminated. · With regard to recommendation 9.1.1: With effect from the start of the year 2002, supervisory visit to the regions will be carried out twice a year in order to improve evaluation of the performance of establishments · With regard to recommendation 9.1.2 first bullet: All egg packing centres intending to export eggs to the EU are authorised and supervised. · With regard to recommendation 9.1.2 second bullet: ­ The absence of Staphylococcus aureus is tested in 1g. (see finding 5.4.4.2 fifth indent). ­ The testing of the three acids mentioned in Chapter VI has commenced, results to date are satisfactory. (see finding 5.4.4.2 sixth indent) · With regard to recommendation 9.1.2 third bullet: Procedures for supervision and procedures for egg products unfit for human consumption are improved in order to prevend that they can be used for human consumption. · With regard to the conclusion 6.3.7.: The health marking has been improved. 24

audits.title: Animal/Public Health General

recommendations.text: To urgently transpose Council Directive 2003/85/EC on community measures for the control of foot-and-mouth disease.
To complete the transposition of Annex A and D of Council Directive 64/432/EEC and to ensure the implementation of their provisions.
To ensure that all eligible animals are tested for tuberculosis, brucellosis and enzootic bovine leucosis in accordance with Annex A and D of Council Directive 64/432/EEC.
To provide the Commission services with correct information on the eradication programme for TB for the years 2001-2003.
To enforce the implementation of the Polish monitoring programme for classical swine fever in wild boars.
To accelerate the registration of the porcine, ovine and caprine holdings.
To ensure that all farm registers are kept in line with Article 8 of Commission Regulation (EC) No 911/2004 and Article 4 of Council Directive 92/102/EEC as amended.
To take urgent action to implement both Commission Regulation (EC) 494/98 and Commission Regulation (EC) 1082/2003.

To ensure that veterinary officials have access to up-to-date information from the database on the number and type of bovine, porcine and ovine/caprine holdings in accordance with Article 3 of Council Directive 92/102/EEC.
To draw up complete and up-to date lists of approved food-processing establishments including their unique approval numbers. 27

To ensure that approval decisions are granted in full accordance with Community legislation and, in the case of transitional period establishments, in accordance with the provisions of the Accession Treaty and subsequent Commission Decisions.

To ensure that only establishments complying with the relevant EU requirements regarding structure, layout, equipment and operational hygiene are approved and that appropriate action is taken with regard to non-compliant establishments.

To re-evaluate establishments with a transitional period and to take into account all the deficiencies regarding structure, layout and equipment in the upgrading plan and to monitor progress accurately.
To enforce Community requirements with regard to food-operators' own-check programmes in food-processing establishments.
To put in place the official supervision required by Article 9 of Council Directive 64/433/EEC in all establishments concerned.
To take action to enforce the health marking and packaging requirements set out in Community legislation.
To introduce measures to ensure that only eligible raw material is accepted into approved food processing establishments.
To enforce the provisions of Regulation (EC) No 1774/2002 on the handling and disposal of animal by-products.
To ensure that supervision over customs warehouses guarantees that they operate in accordance with the requirements of Council Directive 97/78/EC and Commission Decision 2000/571/EC.

To ensure that the food processing establishment in the south of Poland referred to in section 5.8 is approved and supervised in accordance with the Community legislation governing the operations carried out there. The Polish authorities should submit an action plan, detailing the actions taken, and planned, and including deadlines for their implementation to address the above recommendations within one month of receiving the draft report. 9. ADDENDUM In their reply to the English version of the draft report the Polish Competent Authorities outlined the action already taken or planned to address the recommendations made in the draft report. A summary of the main action with regard to each recommendation is given below: 1. Polish legislation adopting the remaining provisions of Council Directive 2003/85/EC will be issued by March 2005. 28 2. Polish legislation transposing all of the provisions of the Annexes of Council Directive 64/432/EC will be issued by March 2005. 3. Veterinary Inspectors have been asked to test all eligible bovine herds, including new-born animals. 4. Results of the eradication programme for TB for the years 2001 to 2003 have been submitted. 5. An Ordinance containing rules and procedures for sampling and monitoring of CSF comes into force on 1 January 2005, veterinary officials have been informed about the necessity of ensuring full implementation of the CSF monitoring programme. 6. In November 2004 an information and training campaign was launched countrywide by ARMA to increase animal keeper's diligence with regard to reporting ovine, caprine and porcine animals for registration. 7. The CCA stated that the correctness of the registers is subject to veterinary controls as well as to ARMA controls and information campaigns. 8. The CA confirmed that the procedures and guidelines for the implementation of Commission Regulation (EC) 494/98 and Commission Regulation (EC) 1082/2003 have been developed and that the respective controls will commence at the beginning of 2005. The Poviat (DVO) Veterinary officials will be in charge of these controls. 9. National legislation is currently in the process of amendment in order to grant improved access to the data held in the database for the Veterinary Inspection services. 10. The CA makes reference to the official website of the Veterinary Inspectorate, which contains these lists. 11. The CVO ensures that approval decisions are granted in full accordance with the respective requirements. 12. The CA states that appropriate action has been taken with regard to non- compliant establishments on the basis of the CVO instruction GIW hig. 500/4/2004 of 1 September 2004. 13. Controls of establishments with a transitional period will take place by mid- 2005, taking into account all deficiencies regarding structure, layout and equipment. 14. A series of training programmes for regional Veterinary Inspection Services is planned and the CVO guarantees that in 2005 own-check programmes in food processing establishments will be emphasised. 15. From 1 January 2005 controls of the proper execution of official supervision as laid down by Article 9 of Council Directive 64/433/EEC shall be emphasised in all establishments approved for trade. 29 16. The CA announced a modification of the Ordinance to transpose the provisions of Council Directive 92/46/EEC into Polish legislation more precisely. Moreover the CA assures that intensified official controls will be carried out to enforce requirements related to health marking and packaging. 17. Additional official controls will be introduced to ensure that only raw material from approved establishments will be accepted in the approved food-processing plants. 18. The CA refers to controls over disposal plants, intermediate establishments, incineration/co-incineration plants, operators collecting dead animals, warehouses for the storage of animal by-products, holdings keeping fur animals and plants manufacturing pet-food. 19. The CVO has ordered the services to pay attention to the respect of the provisions of Council Directive 97/78/EC and Commission Decision 2000/571/EC in warehoused under Veterinary Inspectorate supervision. The CA confirmed that the irregularities in the warehouse operation had been corrected immediately. 20. The CA indicated general measures with regard to State Sanitary Inspection (SSI) controls over food of animal origin used in the production of the establishments under State Sanitary Inspection. Any incidence of poor quality or documentary shortcomings are to be reported directly to the Veterinary Inspection Services. 30

audits.title: Rabies eradication programme

recommendations.text: Follow an appropriate vaccination strategy in certain parts of the country to take account of local risk factors such as a high fox population density or persistence of the disease.
Adapt vaccine distribution arrangements in accordance with the Scientific Committee's recommendations.
Introduce checks on vaccines at the distribution stage.
Ensure improved coordination of activities relating to the oral 2 immunisation of foxes, both at inter-regional level and with the authorities of neighbouring countries.
Take the necessary steps to ensure that testing is carried out on the minimum number of foxes required to monitor the vaccination campaigns.

Make the necessary arrangements to ensure that all measures decided on in the rabies eradication plan for their area are indeed carried out. An action plan describing the action taken or planned in response to the findings and conclusions in this report, and setting out a timetable, must be presented to the Commission within two months of receipt of the final report. ADDENDUM In their letter of 5 April 2005, the Polish authorities described to the FVO the action planned and taken to remedy the shortcomings noted in the report: · Recommendation 1: The new vaccination strategy for 2005 provides for the distribution of 35 baits per km² in areas with a high fox population density. · Recommendation 2: Reducing the distance between flight lines would increase the cost of bait placement and require extra funding, which is practically impossible. However, at the meeting with the heads of the Regional Veterinary Offices (RVO) on 15-16 February 2005, the Chief Veterinary Officer (CVO) recommended reducing the distance between flight lines for the 2005 campaigns. · Recommendation 3: Vaccines undergo initial serial control and control of marketing conditions. Temperature upon delivery is checked during distribution, prior to loading the aircraft, and some random samples are also taken and sent to the NRL to check virus titre. · Recommendation 4: In accordance with the legislation in force, at least 10 days prior to immunisation, the head of the RVO informs the RVOs of neighbouring regions of the date and type of immunisation. At the meeting between CVOs from Poland and Ukraine held on 19-20 February 2005, Poland was asked to help establish an 80-km- wide rabies immunisation corridor in Ukraine; a meeting with Ukrainian experts has been arranged for mid-year to draw up a suitable programme. · Recommendation 5: The number of foxes supplied for monitoring has been increasing since 2002. The CVO recommended that all regions which had not met their monitoring targets should cooperate more effectively with the regional sections of the Polish Hunters' Union. Furthermore, a reward of 25 zlotys had been introduced for every fox culled and handed over. · Recommendation 6: The CVO organises meetings with the heads of the RVOs every two months, at which, amongst other things, matters relating to rabies vaccination campaigns are discussed. The Office for Animal Health and Protection at the Veterinary Inspectorate General organises a quarterly meeting with regional inspectors responsible for animal health, at which the vaccination strategy for the current year and the results of monitoring are analysed. 3

audits.title: Artificial Insemination/Embryo and Semen collection centres

recommendations.text: To notify the Commission services of all approved semen collection and storage centres (Article 5, point 2 of Council Directive 88/407/EEC as amended) and to review the corresponding approval numbers.

To inform the Commission services of the characteristics and form of the marking of doses used in Poland (Annex A, chapter II, point 2 (e) (vi) of Council Directive 88/407/EEC as amended) and to ensure their effective application in all approved SCCs and SSCs.

To ensure that adequate measures are implemented in SCCs and SSCs in the event of a positive result of health tests on the bulls (Annex B, chapter I points (d) and (f); and Annex B, chapter II, point 3 of Council Directive 88/407/EEC as amended).
To ensure that pre-quarantine and quarantine testing of the bulls are carried out in accordance with Annex B of Council Directive 88/407/EEC, as amended.

To ensure that records of all movement of semen and of the health status of the donor bulls are kept and supervised in all semen storage centres (Annex A, chapter II, point 2 (a) of Council Directive 88/407/EEC as amended). 9.3. To provide training for the official veterinarians involved in the inspection of semen collection or storage centres, and to all centre veterinarians on the implementation of Council Directive 88/407/EEC as amended. The Polish authorities should submit an action plan indicating the actions taken and planned in response to the conclusions a s of this report, within one month of receipt of the final version of this report. 17 ADDENDUM The Polish CCA offered by means of a letter dated 10 December comments on the draft report. The Polish authorities gave some clarification and additional information on the findings and conclusions of the draft report, in particular, regarding the labelling of the semen doses, the registration of SCCs and the animal health status of the bulls during the pre-quarantine and quarantine period of bulls in SCCs. In their response to the draft report, the CCA comments on the recommendations, which they are reviewing at present. Actions to rectify some findings are also described. 18

audits.title: Import Controls - Food of Plant Origin

recommendations.text: Fully ensure compliance of official foodstuffs laboratories with Council Directive 93/99/EEC, Article 3.1 and 3.2 in terms of application of standard operating procedures for sample preparation and participation in proficiency tests.
Fully ensure that validation of methods for sample preparation complies with the requirements of the Annex to Council Directive 85/591/EEC16.

Proceed with efforts to accredit official foodstuffs laboratories and implementation of validated methods for analysis in the area of 3-MCPD and Sudan red contamination without delay and ensure the inclusion of a 16 OJ L 372, 31/12/1985, p. 50 - 52 26 number of matrices in accredited methods for the analysis of aflatoxin contamination.

Ensure that the rate of recovery and uncertainty as stated in analytical reports is in compliance with Commission Directive 98/53/EC, Annex 2. Written assurances should be forwarded to the European Commission with regard to the above recommendations within two months of receipt of the final translated mission report. The Competent Authority should provide detailed information on the actions that will be taken and propose deadlines by which these actions will be completed. 9. ADDENDUM In their response to the draft report, the Polish Authorities provided comments and clarifications. Actions to be taken in response to the recommendations made in the report were not indicated yet. 27

audits.title: Food Hygiene

recommendations.text: Ensure that the requirements of Article 3.2 of Council Directive 93/43/EEC are applied to butchers shops which adjoin cutting or processing plants. 20
Ensure that all guides to Good Hygiene Practice meet the requirements of Council Directive 93/43/EEC and are notified to the Commission services.
Continue with plans to ensure that all laboratories approved for the official control of foodstuffs comply with the requirements laid down by Article 3 of Council Directive 93/99/EEC.
Ensure that the laboratories approved for the official control of foodstuffs are notified to the Commission as required by Article 15 of Council Directive 89/397/EEC.
Ensure that the inspection frequency targets established in the national control plan are met at local level (Poviat).
Ensure that food business operators implement food safety procedures based on HACCP principles as required by Article 3 of Council Directive 93/43/EEC.
Ensure that inspectors assess the potential food safety hazards associated with the business as required by Article 8.2 of Council Directive 93/43/EEC.
Continue with plans to ensure that all inspectors at local level are adequately trained to assess the quality systems based on HACCP principles.

Confirm for the final report whether the targets have been met for the 2004 sampling plan. A programme in response to these recommendations should be forwarded to the Commission Services within a period of two months after the receipt of the final report.
ADDENDUM In their response to the draft report the Polish Authorities have not yet addressed the recommendations of the report. 21

audits.title: Import Controls and Border Inspection Posts

recommendations.text: To consider the approval of the IC 2 in Gdynia as separate BIP and to limit the approval to packed products only (HC-T(FR)(2)) depending on the guarantees received in relation to the correct of the deficiencies found. 15 9. ADDENDUM TO MISSION REPORT DG(SANCO)/7594/2005 In response to the recommendations in the draft report, the CAs indicated the followi s under point 8: With regard to the findings or deficiencies detected during the mission carried out last February, CCA have begun to rectify some of the general problems. (1) Directive 99/2002/EC and the provisions for the implementation of Regulation 998/2002/EC were transposed into Polish law by the Act dated 7 January 2005 amending the Act on the protection of animal health and on combating infectious diseases in animals, and amending various other acts (Official Gazette No 23, item 188) and by the Decree of the "Minister of Agriculture and Rural Development" dated 6 April 2005 concerning the production and placing on the market of various products of animal origin (currently being published in the Official Gazette). The provisions of Decision 2000/571/EC were incorporated into the CVO Instruction No GIWbip-2/2005 of 28 January 2005, as amended by Instruction No GIWbip-3/2005 of 28 February 2005.

Polish statutory provisions regarding veterinary border controls have been brought fully into line with Community legislation, and the Tables of Correspondence relating to the legal acts concerned have been accepted by the European Commission. The GVI has made every effort to ensure their proper implementation and enforcement in accordance with the recommendations of the FVO.

The CVO asked the "Ministry of Environment", by letter dated on 18 April (ref. GIWbip 20), to make some essential changes comprising the removal from the register of those border crossings where it is not possible to check live animals, and to leave only the possibility of CITES products being imported through them. The updated list is being sent to all Border Veterinary Officers and to the Head of Customs with the request that it be forwarded to the territorially competent Customs Departments at the border crossing points on the EU's external border.

The draft Decree of the "Minister of Agriculture and Rural Development" concerning a list of border crossing points at which customs bodies carry out checks on pets accompanying travellers and being transported for non- commercial purposes, and concerning the conditions and type of cooperation between customs bodies and District Veterinary Officers in the performance of those checks, is currently at the interdepartmental consultation stage. It is scheduled for publication in the Official Gazette in the first half of June 2005.

The GVI has drawn up training themes for official veterinarians working at BIPs and a training schedule for 2005. The subjects cover Community and national legislation in the field of border veterinary controls, as well as the Code of Administrative Procedure. The CVO has submitted an application to the TAIEX Bureau for the financing of practical training of official veterinarians at border crossing points in other Member States on a study-visit basis. Applications have also been submitted for the organisation of training in the form of workshops. From 18 to 21 and from 25 to 28 April 2005, training is being held for official veterinarians in the fields of equine identification, registration and welfare. The participants are six veterinarians from six BIPs approved for checks on category E animals and two members of staff from the Border Office of the GVI. 16

A working meeting was held at the "Ministry of Finance" on 8 March and 15 April 2005 of central and local representatives of the Customs Service and representatives of the GVI, the "Inspectorate for the Commercial Quality of Agricultural Food Products" and the "Sanitary Inspectorate". The purpose of the meeting was to identify all problems relating to cooperation between all the services carrying out checks at border crossing points. The Border Veterinary Officers were obliged by the CVO to organise similar meetings at local level, with the minutes of those meetings having to be submitted to the CVO. Customs have been provided with the current list of goods which are subject to veterinary inspection (Decision 2002/349). After CVO request in letter (ref. GIWbip 15, dated 16.02.2005) work on inclusion of the list of goods in the ISZTAR-II and CELINA system has already started, and the CVO will be notified as soon as the work has been completed. The question of cooperation in the field of checks on travellers' luggage will be settled under the agreement drawn up between the Head of Customs and the CVO. The CVO also sent a letter (dated 25 February, ref. GIWbip 403/mk-14/2005) to the Head of Customs proposing that joint training be organised relating to border checks on pets in accordance with the Act of 7 January 2005 amending the Act on the protection of animal health and on combating infectious diseases in animals and amending various other acts (Official Gazette No 23, item 188). Training of this kind has already been organised by the Border Veterinary Officers at a number of border crossing points, including at Warsaw Okecie Airport and the road border crossing point at Dorohusk and Bezledy. The training organised by the GVI and the Customs Department of the "Ministry of Finance" is scheduled for the last week of May. There will be 15 participants designated by the "Ministry of Finance" and the District Veterinary Officers territorially responsible for border crossing points at which checks are carried out on pets from third countries. In the Gynia and Bezledy the veterinary inspectors are allowed to open consignments without presence of the customs officer.

The GVI Border Office has drawn up a schedule of checks to be carried out in 2005 at the BIPs and customs warehouses approved for the inspection of products not meeting EU import requirements. They are to be carried out by Border Office inspectors either independently or in conjunction with staff of the GVI Inspections Office. In line with the recommendations made by the FVO, an amended Instruction of the Chief Veterinary Officer, GIWbip1/2005, has been issued, setting out the rules for granting and withdrawing approval for veterinary border inspection posts Concerning the BIP in the Port of Gdansk the CCA provided the information that these facilities are nearly completed, and in May 2005 the building will be inspected for acceptance by the individual departments and handed over for the use of the Border Veterinary Officer. On 12 April 2005, a GVI representative made an inspection visit after which comments a s were sent to the investor

On 11-12 April 2005, checks were carried out on customs warehouses in Gdynia included on the official list of warehouses approved for non-EU conforming products. The checks were performed by inspectors from the GVI 17 Border Office, with the participation of representatives of the Regional and District Veterinary Inspectorates. A post-inspection report was drawn up specifically addressing all the deficiencies noted and ordering their rectification by the end of May 2005. All approval decisions issued by the District Veterinary Officer for customs warehouses coming under his supervision were examined by the GVI Organisational and Legal Office for compliance with Community and national law. It is planned to carry out checks on all remaining customs warehouses and to organise training in the second half of May jointly with the customs services in the port of Gdynia with the aim of exchanging information on the subject of management and supervision of customs warehouses in general and, in particular, of customs warehouses, free customs zones and entities providing means of international transport within the meaning of veterinary and customs law. Every company engaged in supplying vessels with non-EU-conforming products has been informed about the need to obtain approval from GVI. There are currently no suppliers who use non-EU-conforming products for supplying international means of transport.

A plan for monitoring residues, pathogens and contaminants in products of animal origin imported from third countries and intended for use as foodstuffs has been drawn up in accordance with Regulation No 136/2004 by the GVI. Also drawn up was a plan for monitoring residues, contaminants and pathogens in animal feed. It was sent to the BIPs by letter of 18 April (ref. GIWpuf.512pi/50/2005)

The majority of deficiencies noted for facilities, equipment, hygiene, documentation, registration and records in Gdynia and Bezledy have been rectified, and the remaining ones will be eliminated by the deadline set by the FVO. Detailed information was given in Annex 1 of the letter GIW ie 860/13a BIP/2005 dated on 25 April 2005.

The majority of deficiencies noted in IC 2 at the port Gdynia have been rectified, and the remaining ones will be eliminated by the deadline set by the FVO. Detailed information was given in Annex 1 of the letter GIW ie 860/13a BIP/2005 dated on 25 April 2005.

Under the planned BIP inspections, detailed checks will be carried out in Kuznica Bialostocka, Kukuryki/Koroszczyn and Warsaw Okecie airport to confirm that all deficiencies noted in the FVO report 7011/2004 concerning infrastructure for live animals are rectified.

The CVO requested in letter to the chairman of the Gdynia port Baltic Container Terminal on 15 April 2005 (ref. GIWbip 44) that the electronic database on COCONS consignments be made accessible in relation to: container documents, container history, requests for manifest, companies, CARGO LIST, Cargo list issued on board, MANIFEST, Manifest ­ Received from the ship, Notified on board. According to the information received, the database may be used under supervised conditions, with printout but with no updating or input of data into the system. The first part of the CVED is given by the transport company as pre-notification which is carefully inspected by a veterinary officer. According to the information provided by the Customs Department of the Ministry of Finance 18 that pre-notification to Customs of incoming consignments (goods notification) will be possible as from 1 January 2006, following the entry into force of new European customs rules.
The CCA did not indicate a response to the recommendation concerning checks of the products of non-animal origin except hay and straw.

An amended version of the Border Veterinary Officers' Manual was drawn up at the Border Office and sent to all BIPs as a set of guidelines for the conduct of inspections by official veterinarians. As part of the inspection process, all deficiencies or matters of doubt are the subject of ongoing correction on the basis of post-inspection reports.

Jointly with the Ministry of Finance, the GVI has drawn up the wording of an agreement between the CVO and the Head of Customs setting out the rules governing checks on the travellers' luggage of travellers from third countries in accordance with Regulation No 745/2005. Under the agreement, it is the customs services which check travellers' luggage for imported products of animal origin. Seized foodstuffs are placed in locked seized-goods containers which are clearly marked as such. The customs services send information on seized products to the territorially competent District or Border Veterinary Officer. The manager of the border crossing point is responsible for sending the contents of the seized-goods containers to category II disposal facilities. The CVO has also sent a letter to the Chairman of the National Tourist Council at the Ministry of Economy and Labour with the aim of informing tourist organisations about requirements relating to the import of animal-origin products in travellers' luggage. The Embassies of Belarus, Russia and the Ukraine have been informed, and a multimedia presentation has been placed on the official GVI website. On 14 March 2005, an agreement was signed between the Director of the Customs Department at Bezledy and the Border Veterinary Officer "concerning activities relating to checks on the import of animal-origin products in travellers' luggage". On 3 February 2005, the Border Office sent updated posters complying with Regulation No 745/2004 to the Warminsko-Mazurskie Regional Authority in Olsztyn, which forwarded them to the manager of the border crossing point at Bezledy. The posters were put up at the border crossing point in the first half of March 2005. In order to organise checks on travellers' luggage at border crossings where there is no approved BIP, the CVO sent a letter dated 25 February (ref. GIWbip 19) to the territorially competent Regional Veterinary Officers with a view to information being passed on to the District Veterinary Officers and appropriate agreements with the customs services being signed.

The CVO has written to all Border Veterinary Officers (ref. GIWbip 30) instructing them to stop accepting heath certificates for products of animal origin which are in transit or coming from temporary storage on the EU territory and which do not satisfy the standards applying since 1 January 2005. The procedures have been amended and consignments from Russia to third countries are not dispatched under the same conditions as transit within Russia. 19

The Border Veterinary Officer at Bezledy has terminated the waste-disposal contract with the incinerator facility of the District Hospital, because it did not have approval for the processing of category 1 materials. A new agreement is to be signed on 1 June 2005 with a production and trading company , which is approved for the processing of category 1 materials under Regulation (EC) No 1774/2002. The other BIPs have waste-disposal agreements exclusively with operators approved under Regulation (EC) No 1774/2002. Inspection of kitchen waste from international means of transport is performed by the "Environmental Protection Department of the Marine Board". The district Veterinary Officer receives a report from the Marine Board on the volume of waste which has been delivered to an approved storage site and its copy is forwarded to the Border Veterinary Officer. .

audits.title: Potatoes

recommendations.text: Modify Article 5.2 of the regulation of the Minister for Agriculture and Rural Development of 05.08.2004 as amended, including the provision for the 18 bioassay test, in order to fully comply with the EPPO Standard "S. endobioticum: soil tests and de-scheduling of previously infested plots", PM 3/59 (1).

Complete as a matter of priority the registration of producers, warehouses and packing stations as laid down in Commission Directive 92/90/EEC, and start on the routine activity of updating the register of producers.
Promote the use of certified seed by potato producers. The specific project in preparation could be an important contribution to the ring rot control.

Promote the testing of farm-saved seed before planting and the adoption of supplementary hygiene measures (e.g. disinfection of premises, warehouses, stores and vehicles). The competent authorities in Poland should consider:

Reviewing the statistical model for calculating the number of fields to be sampled to establish powiats pest-free and, if appropriate, increasing the sampling in the powiats where the proportion of infested fields was low.

Improving the coordination between the SPHSIS, the Research Centre for Cultivar Testing and the Plant Breeding and Acclimatisation Institute in order to give priority to testing varieties of unknown resistance to S. endobioticum already in use in Poland under the special procedure. Poland is requested to report to the Commission, two months after receipt of the final report, on the actions taken and/or planned in response to the recommendations. A deadline for completion should be indicated for each action. Addendum The Polish Single Authority made comments to the draft report; these are published separately. An initial response to recommendation 1) was also provided, informing that "the required changes have already been included in the draft proposal of the new version of the regulation, and the amending procedure has already been started (letter to the MARD of 14th June 2005, ref. no: WF-070/44/05)". . 19

audits.title: Animal/Public Health General

recommendations.text: To ensure that periodic establishment inspections from RVO and DVO also include proper supervision of the work carried out by lower level CA.

To improve the monitoring of the databases for cattle, sheep/goats and pigs ensuring that the system established gives guarantees that events are notified within the timeframe required by the legislation in force.
To ensure that identification controls in bovine holdings are carried out in accordance with the requirements of Commission Regulation No. (EC) 1082/2003 and Commission Regulation No. (EC) 494/98.

To re-evaluate coldstores in order to ensure that only establishments complying with the relevant EU requirements are approved and that appropriate action is taken with regard to non-compliant establishments.
To correct the shortcomings noted in meat hygiene practices.
To amend the incorrect transposition of Council Directive 64/433/EEC in regard to health marking requirements for carcasses.
To urgently finalise the transposition of Council Directive 2003/85/EC.
To ensure that approval and supervision of all assembly centres and dealers is guaranteed and performed in accordance with the provisions of Council Directives 64/432/EEC and 91/68/EEC.
To update the contingency plans for FMD and CSF in order to ensure full compliance with Council Directives 2003/85/EC and 2001/89/EC.

To adapt the contingency plans, in particular FMD and CSF, to the local conditions of regions and districts as required by Council Directives 2003/85/EC and 2001/89/EC, and to correct the deficiencies detected.

To ensure that equipment stored at DVO and system in place for supply of additional equipment can guarantee its full availability for detection of outbreak and eradication of disease, as required by Council Directives 2003/85/EC and 2001/89/EC.
To ensure the accurate and prompt updating of CDB and incorporate system tools required for full traceability of animals in case of a disease outbreak.

To ensure that training, simulation exercises and awareness in relation to contingency plans, in particular FMD and CSF, is carried out regularly as required by Council Directives 2001/89/EC and 2003/85/EC. 20 ADDENDUM Response of the Polish Authorities to the draft mission report The Polish Authorities commented on the draft report by means of a letter dated 30 January 2006. Where appropriate these comments have been incorporated into the final report. They also provided an initial reaction to certain conclusions a s in the report, in particular by providing details of action already taken or to be taken to correct deficiencies noted.

audits.title: Animal Welfare on farms

recommendations.text: To correctly transpose and/or take measures to bring into effect: (a) The provision, where appropriate, of dry comfortable bedding to sick or injured animals (Annex to Directive 98/58/EC, point 4). (b) The maintenance of a record of the number of mortalities found at each inspection (Annex to Directive 98/58/EC, point 5).
To transpose Directive 2002/4/EC concerning the registration of establishments with laying hens covered by Directive 99/74/EC.
To take measures to ensure that sanctions have the necessary effect of discouraging offenders (Directive 91/630/EEC, Article 11 (1) and Directive 99/74/EC, Article 13).
To provide sufficient staff at central level, in particular to provide guidance, updating this as necessary and co-ordinating activities in relation to animal welfare.
To further develop the regional supervision of district level in order to improve the quality of animal welfare inspections and reporting of results.

In relation to the pig sector, to take steps to ensure that: 10 (a) Appropriate instructions and guidance are available to both farmers (Directive 91/630/EEC, Article 5a) and those carrying out checks, in particular on group housing of pregnant sows, bulky feed for pregnant sows, tail-docking, castration and appropriate materials for manipulation. (b) The requirement for permanent access to fresh water (Annex to Directive 91/630/EEC, Chapter I, (7)) is respected.

To take measures to ensure that an adequate methodology is adopted for the inspection of holdings and that appropriate equipment is available to measure space allowance and parameters such as light, noise and adequacy of ventilation.

In relation to laying hens, re-assess farms which have been already inspected, in particular in relation to space allowance (Directive 99/74/EC, Article 5, (1) point 1.1) and where overstocking is detected, dissuasive actions should be taken.

Regarding the reporting of infringements (Decision 2000/50/EC), take steps to ensure that: (a) All infringements are classified correctly. (b) When more than one deficiency is detected on the same holding, all the categories infringed are reported. 9. ADDENDUM TO MISSION REPORT DG/(SANCO)/7638/2005 In their comments on a draft version of this report, the central competent authority provided an action plan to address the recommendations as follows: 1) In relation to recommendation (1) that they propose to amend the Decree of 13 September 2005 amending the Decree on the minimum living conditions of individual species of farm animals. 2) In reply to recommendation (2) that the Chief Veterinary Officer addressed a letter on 15 July 2005 to the District Veterinary officers requesting them to keep registers of farms producing eggs for human consumption. 3) In relation to recommendation (3), that the Chief Veterinary Officer addressed a letter to the Minister of Agriculture and Rural Development recommending to amend the Act of 21 August 1997 on the Protection of Animals in order to introduce the possibility of using administrative sanctions to punish animal welfare infringements. 4) In reply to recommendation (4), that, from 19 December 2005, the Office of Health and Protection of Animals of the General Veterinary Inspectorate will employ an additional Senior Inspector who is responsible for animal protection issues. 5) In relation to recommendation (5), that new check-lists for animal welfare inspections have been revised by the General Veterinary Inspectorate and 11 will be presented to the Voivodship Inspectors at a meeting on animal protection held on 21-22 February 2006. 6) In reply to recommendation (6), that the Chief Veterinary Officer addressed a letter on 30 January 2006 to Veterinary Officers requesting them to ensure during their inspections that pigs which are more than 2 weeks old have permanent access to water and that castration and tail docking are performed in compliance with the law. The letter also contained an information leaflet targeted at pig keepers and instructed inspectors of farms to distribute it in pig farms. 7) In relation to recommendation (7), that the Chief Veterinary Officer addressed a letter on 5 December 2005 to the Minister of Agriculture and Rural Development asking financial provisions to buy appropriate equipment. 8) In reply to recommendation (8), that the Chief Veterinary Officer will send an instruction to inspect again laying hen farms with more than 350 hens kept in cage system as soon as the new check-list for inspection of farms is approved and to ensure compliance with space allowance. 9) In relation to recommendation (9), that the Chief Veterinary Officer amended his earlier instruction of 31 May 2005 to ensure that all infringements related to "mutilations" will be correctly classified and that all deficiencies will be reported when more than one deficiency is detected on the same farm. 12

audits.title: Pesticides

recommendations.text: The competent authorities should establish a simplified procedure for the authorisation of parallel imports of PPPs, in order to comply with the judgement of case C-100/96 of the European Court of Justice.

Existing authorisations should be routinely reviewed in cases where new MRLs have been set, to ensure that the authorised use of plant protection products does not lead to an MRL infringement or risk to consumer health.
The competent authorities should ensure that the annual report to the Commission, in the framework of Article 17 of Council Directive 91/414/EEC, includes results of all the inspection measures.

The competent authorities should consider strengthening the level and depth of enforcement, particularly in the area of control of users of plant protection products in accordance with Article 17 of Council Directive 91/414/EEC.

The competent authorities should identify the exact quantities of obsolete pesticides in "tombs", warehouses, farms and at manufacturers, and co-ordinating 20 activities for their supervision and safe destruction, in order to avoid possible contamination of food, feed and the environment.

Accreditation of the laboratories carrying out pesticide residue analysis should be finalised. The laboratories should take measures to avoid possible cross- contamination between standards and samples, carry out regular recovery tests, and support the reported limits of determination by recovery data. The procedure for sample preparation should ensure that the analytical portion is representative, as required by point 4.8 of the Annex of Commission Directive 2002/63/EC.

The competent authorities should continue to increase the range of pesticides and metabolites in the analytical screens, so as to better reflect those substances being marketed and to ensure adequate enforcement of pesticide MRLs as specified in Council Directives 76/895/EEC, 86/362/EEC and 90/642/EEC as amended.

The competent authorities should reduce the time-lapse between sampling for pesticide residues analysis and reporting of results as to allow adequate enforcement and follow-up actions, as well as any necessary emergency measures.

The competent authorities should ensure that all cases of MRL breaches are notified to qualified staff for consumer risk assessment. An action plan in response to the recommendations should be forwarded to the Commission within 2 months of dispatch of the final translated report. This action plan should clearly set out the manner and deadline by which the competent authorities will address each recommendation. 9. ADDENDUM In their response to the draft report the Polish authorities provided corrections and clarifications. This response did not yet provide a response to the recommendations. 21

audits.title: Plant passport system

recommendations.text: Notification, according to Article 12 of Directive 2000/29/EC, is made to the Member State concerned and to the Commission when regulated articles are moved within the Community without a valid plant passport. The single authority in Poland should consider:

Revising the sampling methods for Globodera pallida and G. rostochiensis in order to comply with that described in the EPPO standard "Phytosanitary procedures Globodera pallida & G. rostochiensis- Soil sampling methods PM 3/30 (1). Poland is requested to report to the Commission, two months after receipt of the final report, on the action taken and/or planned on the recommendations. For planned action, a deadline should be indicated. 10. ADDENDUM The Polish Single Authority made comments to the draft report; these are published separately. 18

audits.title: BSE AND ANIMAL NUTRITION

recommendations.text: To ensure that there is sufficient staff at various levels in order to deliver a sufficient frequency of official controls in the field of animal nutrition. With regard to BSE epidemio-surveillance
To bring the definition of TSE suspicion in national legislation in line with Art. 3 1 (h) of Regulation (EC) No 999/2001.
To take further steps to ensure a feasible tracing of animals subject to an inquiry to identify all animals at risk, as required in Art. 13 of Regulation (EC) No 999/2001.
To ensure that autolysed samples, notably those originating from fallen bovines, are tested as required in Annex X, Chapter C, (3).1 to Regulation (EC) No 999/2001.

To ensure that the monitoring of the testing programme is based on accurate and reliable information and implemented correctly, in order to confirm that the level of testing as set out in Annex III to Regulation (EC) No 999/2001 is achieved and to allow timely corrective actions. With regard to SRM

To ensure that the harvesting of head meat is in compliance with the requirements laid down in Annex XI, Chapter A to Regulation (EC) No 999/2001/EC and that appropriate controls are in place. With regard to the total feed ban
To ensure that national provisions on the flow of organic fertilizers are properly enforced, in order to have a clear picture about their distribution and use.

To ensure that the official control programme is designed taking into account the risks and experience gained, as required in Art. 4 of Directive 95/53/EC, and that the sampling is targeted to points where cross-contamination is most likely to occur. 11 DG(SANCO)/7693/2005 ­ MR Final
To ensure that results of MAT are provided in a timely fashion.

To ensure that effective penalties are imposed in proportion to their purpose and that they have a deterrent effect where failure of compliance with rules is detected, as required in Art. 19 of Directive 95/53/EC.

To ensure that home compounders using feedingstuffs containing fishmeal with more than 50% crude protein for the production of complete feedingstuffs are authorised in accordance with Annex IV, Chapter II (B) to Regulation (EC) No 999/2001. With regard to official inspections in the field of animal nutrition
To draw up a national control programme taking into account the risks and experience gained and specifying the criteria used in accordance with Art. 4 and 22 of Directive 95/53/EC, respectively.

To ensure that feeding stuffs are checked for the presence of certain substances, (notably unauthorised medicinal substances and mycotoxins), as recommended in the EU coordinated inspection programmes in the field of animal nutrition. With regard to approval and registration of E/I
To ensure that all approved operators have been assigned with relevant approval numbers, as required in Art. 5 of Directive 95/53/EC, notably home compounders.

To ensure that all feed operators are aware of the requirements under Directive 95/69/EC. 12 DG(SANCO)/7693/2005 ­ MR Final ADDENDUM RESPONSE OF THE CA TO THE RECOMMENDATIONS Comments from the Polish CCA on the draft report were received on 28 November 2005, on 13 December 2005 and 9 January 2006, and included an outline of the actions planned and/or undertaken to address certai s contained in the report: These may be summarised as follows: With regard to BSE epidemio-surveillance 2. The GVI has requested the MARD to bring the definition of a TSE suspicion in national legislation in line with Art.3 (1) h of Regulation (EC) No 999/2001. 3. In cooperation with the ARiMR, the GVI has defined a series of requests to the identification database to establish the reasons for the discrepancies between the GVI and ARiMr data. This will aim to establish the reasons for delays arising between notifications of information on fallen stock and testing and disposing of the animals. 5. Routine cross-checking will be enhanced, making it possible to establish if samples submitted can be matched with the results. With regard to SRM 6. The GVI requested the NRL to draft a testing methodology and a monitoring programme to meet the requirements of the sampling programme on harvested head meat. These measures have not yet been finalised. With regard to the total feed ban and to official inspections in the field of animal nutrition 7. The GVI requested an amendment to the provisions of the Regulation concerning the use of soil improvers which is due to come into effect in the first quarter of 2006. 6. The 2006 national control programme will be based on the Commissio s, the results of monitoring in 2004 and 2005, the scale of animal feed stuff production in individual voivodships and a detailed risk analysis. The number of animal feed samples taken to test for PAP will be increased by 100% in 2006. A handbook for powiat veterinary officers concerning risk analysis has been prepared, allowing the introduction of an effective feed sampling programme at points where cross-contamination is likely to occur. The provisions of Art. 22 of Directive 95/53/EC will be incorporated in the national control programme prepared. 7. The veterinary health offices conducting MAT testing are requested to reduce the necessary time to test for the presence of PAP in animal feedingstuffs, and powiat veterinary officers will be notified by phone in the event of positive results. 8. The GVI has requested the MARD to amend the Act on animal feedinstuffs by introducing higher fines for the illegal use of PAP in feedingstuffs. The Act is due to come into force in the first quarter of 2006. 9. All home compounders producing feed including fish meal and comprising more than 50 % of crude protein will be authorised and recorded in a register kept at powiats pursuant to Annex IV, Chapter II, (B) to Regulation (EC) No 999/2001. 10. Pursuant to the Commissio , all myxotoxins will be controlled in 2006, and the number of veterinary medicinal substances tested will be increased to 11. 13 DG(SANCO)/7693/2005 ­ MR Final With regard to approval and registration of E/I 11. The powiat veterinary officers are recommended to assign approval numbers to home compounders. 12. All the powiat veterinary officers are encouraged to provide the feed manufacturers with copies of the handbook for feed producers, which might be placed on the GVI webpage. __________________ 14

audits.title: Import Controls and Border Inspection Posts

recommendations.text: To consider the approval of the BIPs - Gdansk port: HC(2), NHC(2), - Dorohusk road: HC, NHC-NT, NHC-T(FR), O and - Terespol-Kobylany: HC, NHC if satisfactory guarantees in relation to the rectification of the deficiencies found are received.

To change the approval of the listed IC 2 of Gdynia port to - HC-T(FR)(2). 11 9. ADDENDUM TO MISSION REPORT DG(SANCO)/7728/2005 In response to the recommendations in Annex 3 to the draft report, the CAs indicated the following measures taken to rectify deficiencies: 1. As regards decision 2005/755 amending Decisions 2005/92 and 2005/93 Chief Veterinary Officer on 24 November 2005 issued an official letter to Regional (Voivod) Veterinary Officers informing about new requirements concerning presence of written permit of acceptance the consignments by the competent authority in third country of destination. The information was passed to all District Veterinary Officers supervising customs warehouses approved in accordance with article 12 Dir. 97/78. The copy of the letter was given to FVO inspectors during the closing meeting. 2. The list of CITES entry points has been corrected accordingly to Commission Decision 349/2002 and the updated list was sent to the Ministry of Environment, letter GIWbip/403/1-06/ps of 4 January 2006.

On 30, 31 January and 1 February 2006 there will be the workshop held in Warsaw arranged by GVI and TAIEX Office. The scope of the training is to familiarize official veterinarians working in BIPs with import rules and procedures of products of animal origin (30, 31 January) and live animals (1 February). The workshop includes also training on TRACES system and general overview of Regulation 882/2004 and similarities and differences between 882/2004 and Dir. 97/78. As regards the import control of live animals it is foreseen to discuss Regulation 998/2003, Dir. 92/65, 91/496 and relevant legislation concerning importation of equidae, exotic birds, non- harmonised species of animals, re-import and transhipment of live animals with issuing CVED for live animal. 4./8. CVO will monitor the progress in works with Customs electronic systems where the information concerning veterinary border check requirements (Decision 349/2002) should be implemented to give automatic information for customs officers carrying out the border control. The port system COCONS is now operational in Gdynia BIP. The problem is under discussion between Borders Office in GVI and Customs Chamber in Kraków, where administrator of CELINA system is located. It is also planned to arrange a meeting with competent authorities of the Customs Service in order to establish co-operation rules concerning data exchange. 5./10. Accordingly to the information given by FVO experts during mission in February 2005 it was possible to store conforming and non-conforming goods in one storage room if the goods are clearly marked and stored in separate areas of the room, marked with borderline and names "conforming goods" and "non-conforming goods". Chief Veterinary Officer on 28 December 2005 issued a letter to Regional (Voivod) Veterinary Officers with recommendations for District Veterinary Officers who supervise customs warehouses for non-conforming goods in order to comply with the requirements established in Dir. 97/78 and Decision 2000/571 a s given by the FVO inspectors. The controls in customs warehouses for non-conforming goods held by Borders Office in GVI in 2006 will show the implementation of the measures mentioned above. Chief Veterinary Officer on 27 and 29 December 2005 issued also the letter to Regional (Voivod) Veterinary Officers with recommendations for District Veterinary Officers who supervise customs warehouses for non-conforming goods to report by 20 January 2006 that all the goods introduced into warehouses before 1 January 2005 (non-compliant with specific animal health requirements) have been sent to the place 12 of destination in third country or destroyed in incineration plants. The information will be sent to the Commission, in accordance with the Commission request in the letter E3I-PRO-9778 on 21 December 2005r. 6. GDASK: On 6 January 2006 there was an official application sent to Gdansk Port Authority for access to 2 telephone lines and 1 fax line. ANIMO number was established for Gdansk BIP ­ 2522299, the TRACES login is 2522299@wetgiw.gov.pl. The e-mail address: gdansk.griw@wetgiw.gov.pl; the electronic system for identification and selection of consignments will be established till the end of January 2006. The similar system COCONS is now operational in Gdynia BIP. DOROHUSK: the deficiencies in equipment have been rectified, ie. bird cages, reptile cages, knives, pots etc. Documentation has also been completed: lists of third countries, models of veterinary certificates. Deficiencies in infrastructure have been eliminated and the equipment in inspection and storage rooms has become operational. The notification to the TRACES system has been done. The professional company is providing for the cleaning of facilities and preparation of the appropriate procedures. TERESPOL-KOBYLANY: In the BIP there are three telephone lines available moved from BIP Kukuryki/Koroszczyn. It is settled with Telekomunikacja Polska SA to install and use the Internet connection DSL 1000. It could be activated within 7 days from the date of request to TPSA. The e-mail address is active: terespol.griw@wetgiw.gov.pl. The ANIMO number is established: 2506299. The access to TRACES system is available: login 2506299@wetgiw.gov.pl. PKP SA as an investor started the final technical acceptance works within a special commission. The first meeting will be held in January 2006. There are cleaning works and checking every system in the building carried out (air condition, cooling system, system of control of access to the building etc.). The completion of administrative and technical equipment has been finalized. 7. BEZLEDY: Referring to CVO letter to the Head of Warminsko-Mazurskie Voivodship as a competent authority for administration the infrastructure in border crossing in Bezledy, the reply dated 12 December 2005 was send to GVI informing that the shortcomings concerning live animals zone will be rectified as soon as the founds will be obtained by the Voivod as the budget of Viovodship for 2005 was not large enough to finalize the works. audits.title: Intra Community Trade in live animals

recommendations.text: To ensure that national legislation accords with the requirements of Council Directive 64/432/EEC, particularly regarding the approval of premises used to gather consignments of live animals intended for intra-Community trade.

To fully implement the requirements of Articles 4 and 6 of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004, and in particular to ensure that sufficient numbers of suitably qualified, trained and experienced staff are employed so that official controls and control duties can be carried out efficiently and effectively.
To ensure that official controls are carried out effectively and that corrective actions are taken when needed, in accordance with the requirements of Article 8 of Regulation (EC) No 882/2004.

To ensure that all holdings on which animals are held or kept, in particular collection centres, are registered separately in accordance with Articles 14 and 18 of Council Directive 64/432/EEC and Article 8 of Council Regulation (EC) No 21/2004.

To take immediate measures to prevent the despatch of any animal, and in particular cattle and horses, to another Member State that is not identified in accordance with the provisions of Council Directive 90/426/EEC, Council Directive 92/102/EEC, Regulation (EC) No 1760/2000 of the European Parliament and of the Council and Council Regulation (EC) No 21/2004.

To ensure that the testing regimes adopted for animal diseases, in particular bovine Brucellosis, comply with the requirements of Annexes A and D of Council Directive 64/432/EEC and that the officially disease-free status of herds is suspended if they are not tested within the intervals prescribed.

To urgently review the approval, operation and supervision of all assembly centres and to prohibit the use of collection centres for the purpose of gathering live animals intended for intra-Community trade if they do not meet all of the requirements set out in Article 11 of Council Directive 64/432/EEC.

To ensure that checks are performed on live animals at their destination in accordance with the requirements of Article 5 of Council Directive 90/425/EEC, that the corrective actions set out in Article 6 of that Directive are applied if necessary and that the results of all checks are recorded in the manner prescribed by Commission Regulation (EC) No 599/2004

To take immediate action to ensure that certifying veterinarians comply with the requirements of Council Directive 96/93/EC and that checks or audits are carried out to ensure the integrity of certification and to properly investigate any instances of false or misleading certification which are brought to the attention of the CCA.

To ensure that health inspections of live animals intended for intra- Community trade is performed only by OVs and only on either the holding of origin or in an approved assembly centre, as required by Article 5 of Council Directive 64/432/EEC. 22

To ensure that official controls on all holdings verify that stock farmers and veterinarians record and retain information on veterinary treatments as required by Annex I of Regulation (EC) No 852/2004 and Article 10 of Council Directive 96/23/EC.
